title: fix(uninstall): keep going and exit non-zero when pip uninstall fails in clean/uninstall
body:
Follow-up to #6762 (no separate issue).

### The issue

`pipenv clean` and `pipenv uninstall` check `c.returncode != 0` after `run_command(...)`, but `run_command` raises `PipenvCmdError` on a non-zero exit unless `catch_exceptions=False` is passed. So the check is dead code: the first failing `pip uninstall` aborts with a traceback, the remaining packages are never attempted, and the "failure" return/exit-code path from #6762 is never reached.

### The fix

Pass `catch_exceptions=False` at the two call sites (`pipenv/routines/clean.py`, `pipenv/routines/uninstall.py::_uninstall_from_environment`), so the existing handling runs: `clean` continues with the rest and reports failure, `uninstall` prints the error and returns `False`.

### Validation

- Two new unit tests that exercise the real `run_command` (the existing ones mock it entirely, which hid this): `clean` with two packages whose `pip uninstall` fails must attempt both and return `True`; `_uninstall_from_environment` must return `False` instead of raising.
- Red on `main`: 2 failed, 9 passed. Green on this branch: 11 passed (`tests/unit/test_clean_routine.py`, `tests/unit/test_uninstall_exit_code.py`).

title: fix(scan): preserve Safety stderr on quiet failures

title: fix(requirements): keep markers on VCS entries with --no-lock
body:
Follow-up to #6760 (merged), which kept the markers of VCS entries in the lockfile path; this fixes the same loss in the `--no-lock` path.

### The issue

`pipenv requirements --no-lock` drops the `markers` of Pipfile entries that point to a VCS (`git`, `hg`, `svn`, `bzr`), so `pkg = {git = "...", ref = "...", markers = "sys_platform == 'linux'"}` is emitted without its marker and gets installed on every platform. The lockfile path (`requirement_from_lockfile`) keeps the marker.

### The fix

`requirement_from_pipfile` now computes the markers before the VCS branch and appends them to the direct-reference form (`pkg @ git+url@ref ; marker`), as the lockfile path does. Editable lines are unchanged since pip ignores markers there. `include_markers=False` still omits them.

### Tests

New `tests/unit/test_requirements_vcs_markers.py` (4 cases; 2 fail before the change, all pass after), asserting the output equals `requirement_from_lockfile`'s. Existing `test_requirements_*` unit tests still pass.

title: Fix latent bugs surfaced by CodeQL code quality scan
body:
Addresses the actionable CodeQL Code Quality findings in first-party code. `pipenv/vendor`, `pipenv/patched`, and the third-party submodules under `tests/test_artifacts` and `tests/pypi` are left untouched.

title: fix(graph): draw the tree with characters stdout can encode
body:
### The issue

On Windows, `pipenv graph` fails when its output is piped or redirected, for example `pipenv graph > deps.txt` in cmd, `pipenv graph | Select-String requests` in PowerShell, or a CI job without `PYTHONIOENCODING`. It prints the first top-level package and then exits with 1:

```
  File "...\pipenv\routines\graph.py", line 99, in do_graph
    console.print(f"[bold]{escaped_line}[/bold]")
  ...
UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode characters in position 0-2: character maps to <undefined>
```

`--reverse` and `--bare` fail the same way. This is the `pipenv graph` crash reported in #5929: https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/issues/5929#issuecomment-2253457731

### The fix

`run_command()` sets `PYTHONIOENCODING=UTF-8` for pipdeptree, so pipdeptree always draws the tree with box-drawing characters, and pipenv then prints them to a cp1252 stdout. Run on its own, pipdeptree checks its stdout encoding and falls back to an ASCII tree (`  - certifi [...]`). This passes pipenv's stdout encoding (`console.encoding`) to pipdeptree's `--encoding` option, so redirected output gets the ASCII tree again. A UTF-8 terminal still gets the box-drawing tree, and `--json`/`--json-tree` are unchanged. Forcing pipenv's stdout to UTF-8 or `errors="replace"` would affect every command, so the change stays where the tree is drawn.

The graph integration tests did not catch this because CI sets `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8`. The new unit test uses a cp1252 stdout explicitly.

Ran: `pytest tests/unit` on Windows, Python 3.12 (1882 passed, 9 skipped). The new test fails without the change and passes with it on 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14.
Ran: `ruff check` (0.9.3) and `mypy` (2.4.0) as configured in pre-commit.
Checked: `pipenv graph`, `--reverse`, `--bare`, `--json` and `--json-tree` redirected to a file in cmd and piped in PowerShell all exit 0. `tests/integration/test_cli.py::test_pipenv_graph` fails on main and passes with the change when `PYTHONIOENCODING` is unset.

title: Avoid CodeQL false positive for requirements trusted-host output
body:
### The issue

[Code-scanning alert #27](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/security/code-scanning/27) reports clear-text logging of a secret when `pipenv requirements` emits `--trusted-host`. The SARIF trace starts at the call to `trusted_host_for_source()`. The helper returns only the parsed hostname and optional port; it does not return URL credentials.

This is a naming-based false positive: CodeQL's [sensitive-data heuristic](https://github.com/github/codeql/blob/main/shared/concepts/codeql/concepts/internal/SensitiveDataHeuristics.qll) classifies names containing `trusted` as secrets.

### The fix

Rename the internal helper to `get_insecure_source_host` and its local result to `host_and_port`, updating both requirements export and pip argument construction. Document the reason for the names. Requirements output and credential handling remain unchanged.

Add 10 regression cases checking that `--trusted-host` output excludes literal, encoded, and token-only credentials, as well as query strings and fragments. Cover environment placeholders without expansion, IPv6 with a port, verified sources, hostless URLs, and malformed ports. These cases also passed before the rename, confirming that this addresses a false positive.

title: fix(update): parse package names in update arguments as requirements
body:
`pipenv update` takes the package name from each argument by splitting on `=` / `==`:

- `_detect_conflicts` split `requests[socks]==2.0` into `requests[socks]` and `2.0`, and `pkg>=2` into `pkg>` and `2`. The name never matched a key in the reverse dependencies, so the early conflict check silently did nothing for any argument with extras, and the names weren't normalized either (`My_Package`).
- `_find_additional_categories` and the `explicitly_requested` map used the raw argument (`requests>=2`) as the package name, so a package also present in another lockfile category was not found and not updated there, and the explicit-category guard in `_process_package_args` compared an unnormalized argument with a normalized name.

**Fix:** a small `_requirement_name()` helper parses the name from the argument (extras and specifiers dropped, normalized with `pep423_name`; non-requirement arguments such as URLs keep the previous fallback). `_detect_conflicts` now only checks exact pins (`==`, or the legacy single `=`): a range like `pkg~=2.1` must not be tested as version `2.1`, so ranges are left to the resolver as before. The conflict check itself is unchanged.

Note: conflict detection still can't flag a range such as `pkg>=2` (`check_version_conflicts` only compares exact versions); this PR does not change that.

**Tests** (`tests/unit/test_update.py`): a pinned package with extras and a differently spelled name are now flagged; ranges are not treated as pins; `requests>=2` / `requests[socks]~=2.1` find the other category; the name helper falls back for URLs. Before the change the extras, name-normalization and category-lookup cases fail. `pytest tests/unit/test_update.py tests/unit/test_do_update_context_routing.py`: 37 passed.

A towncrier fragment is included (`news/+update-requirement-names.bugfix.rst`); it needs renaming to the PR number.

title: feat(resolver): add uv resolver backend
body:
Closes #6109.

Adds a `uv` backend to the pluggable resolver registry. Select it with `pipenv lock --backend uv`, `PIPENV_RESOLVER=uv`, or `resolver_backend = "uv"` in the Pipfile's `[pipenv]` section. The default stays `pip`.

## How it works

The backend runs `uv pip compile` against the project's interpreter and translates the output into `Pipfile.lock` entries. It does not use `uv lock`: that resolves for every platform at once and can lock two versions of one package, which `Pipfile.lock` can't represent. `uv pip compile` resolves for a single environment, the same way the pip backend does.

- **uv discovery:** uses the `uv` on `$PATH`; it is not vendored. If uv is missing, locking fails with an install hint and never falls back to pip (per the 2026-05-12 sign-off in `docs/dev/initiative-f-backends-design.md`).
- **Index restriction:** a package without an `index` key resolves only from the first source; a pinned package resolves only from its source. Pins declared in other Pipfile categories are honoured, as in the pip backend. The primary source is passed as `UV_DEFAULT_INDEX` in the environment, because `uv pip compile` ignores `default = true` on indexes declared in its input file. Using the environment rather than `--default-index` keeps URL credentials out of process listings.
- **Hashes:** `--generate-hashes` hashes every file of each locked version, matching the pip backend's coverage.
- **Markers:** markers on Pipfile entries are kept and folded onto the transitive dependencies they introduce. Top-level packages excluded by their markers are still recorded, as the pip backend does.
- **Categories:** non-default categories are constrained by the resolved default dependencies.
- **Auth:** URL credentials, `.netrc`, and `PIPENV_KEYRING_PROVIDER` work. Pip's keyring values are mapped onto uv's `disabled` / `subprocess`.

## Known differences from the pip backend (documented)

- **Requires-Python markers:** the pip backend adds markers like `python_version >= '3.9'` from each package's supported Python range. uv doesn't report that range, so the uv backend omits them. They are always true for the environment that was locked.
- **`file=` dependencies:** only the hash of the pinned file is recorded. The pip backend also adds the index sdist's hash.
- **`--extra-pip-args`:** ignored, with a warning.

## Testing

- **Unit:** `tests/unit/test_uv_backend.py` covers spec translation, pyproject rendering, output parsing, marker folding (including cycles), and the failure paths. The uv subprocess is mocked.
- **Integration:** `tests/integration/test_lock_uv_backend.py` checks pip-vs-uv lockfile parity on the offline `file://` index, plus conflict reporting. It is skipped when uv isn't installed.
- **Manual, real projects:** projects covering extras, markers, git, a pinned PyTorch index, an editable path, a `file=` URL, and dev categories. Locked versions and hashes match the pip backend apart from the differences above, and `pipenv sync` from a uv-produced lockfile installs.
- **Manual, private index:** against a local password-protected index, credentials in the URL and credentials only in `.netrc` both work. With no credentials, locking fails with uv's 401 message.

## CI benchmark

The `Package Manager Benchmark` job now also runs with `uv` (`matrix.backend: [pip, pure-python, uv]`). Like the pure-python job, it installs uv and is non-blocking. Cold-cache operations also run `uv cache clean`, so uv's cold timings start from an empty cache. A local run of Sentry's requirement set locked 145 packages, all with hashes: 2.7s from a cold cache and 0.6s warm, on a Ryzen 9 7950X.

## Not in this PR

- `_meta.resolver_backend` and `--allow-backend-switch` (sign-off answers 5 and 6). These aren't implemented for any backend yet.
- Running the full test suite under both backends in CI (sign-off answer 9). The benchmark job above covers performance only.

## Found along the way (separate issue)

The pip backend's hash collection appears to prefix-match versions. For `typing-extensions==4.16.0` it also records the hashes of the `4.16.0rc1` and `4.16.0rc2` files.

title: Fail fast when integration tests would run a different pipenv
body:
## Problem

Integration tests shell out to `pipenv` from `PATH` (the `_PipenvInstance.pipenv()` helper, plus direct calls in `test_run.py`, `test_cli.py`, and `test_windows.py`). If the test virtualenv doesn't have pipenv installed, that command quietly resolves to some other install, such as a user-level `~/.local/bin/pipenv`. The tests then exercise a different pipenv version than the checkout.

This came up while reviewing #6771. The four `test_sync_installs_only_selected_pylock_groups` cases failed locally on both `main` and the PR branch with group-selection assertion errors. That looked like a real bug, but the cause was a released pipenv on `PATH` that predates the feature. CI isn't affected because it runs `pip install -e ".[tests,dev]"` into the venv.

## Change

An autouse, session-scoped fixture in `tests/integration/conftest.py` runs `pipenv --support` from an empty directory, the same way the tests run, and compares the reported `Pipenv location` with the package the test process imported. If they differ, every integration test fails immediately with:

```
The `pipenv` command on PATH runs /home/user/.local/lib/python3.14/site-packages/pipenv, not the checkout under test (/home/user/pipenv/pipenv).  Install it into the test environment with: pipenv run python -m pip install -e ".[tests,dev]"
```

The check runs from an empty directory because a `PYTHONPATH` with an empty entry (the current directory) can hide the mismatch when the command runs from the repo root.

## Testing

- Without an install in the venv: the guard fires with the message above, instead of the four confusing assertion failures.
- With the checkout importable by the `PATH` pipenv (as in CI): `tests/integration/test_pylock.py` passes 9/9, and `test_run.py` plus `test_cli.py` pass (33 passed, 4 skipped).
- The check adds about 0.5s per worker, once per session.

title: Update security dependency floors and support Python 3.11–3.15
body:
### The issue

The development sections of `Pipfile.lock` and `pylock.toml` still select vulnerable virtualenv and filelock releases, and the old development lock also contains vulnerable setuptools. Updating a lock entry alone would still allow affected releases through Pipenv's published dependency requirements.

This addresses the 19 reported Dependabot alerts: virtualenv #189–195, #197 and #200–206; filelock #199, #207 and #208; and setuptools #198.

### The fix

Require patched dependency versions and regenerate both repository lockfiles:

| Dependency | Minimum required version | Locked version |
| --- | --- | --- |
| virtualenv | 21.14.9 | 21.15.1 |
| filelock | 4.2.1 | 4.2.4 |
| setuptools | 84.1.0 | 84.2.1 |

- **Raise Pipenv's minimum Python version to 3.11.** Patched filelock requires Python 3.11, so filelock now has an explicit dependency floor instead of relying on virtualenv's broader transitive requirement. Apply the setuptools floor to build isolation as well as runtime installation.
- Add Python 3.15 to package classifiers and the Linux/macOS/Windows CI matrix. Python 3.12 remains covered by the smoke job. Update publishing, development/Docker version lists, installation examples and the generated manual.
- Use stdlib `tomllib` directly in two host-side parsers now that Python 3.11 is the minimum, keeping type checking valid at the new minimum.
- Regenerate the locks with current Pipenv, preserving the existing pinned releases for atomicwrites, waitress and legacy-cgi that the Linux/Python 3.11 resolver skips. Verify their platform/Python markers and all published artifact hashes. No files under `pipenv/vendor` or `pipenv/patched` are changed.

The dependency floors cover the [virtualenv security fixes](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/security/advisories/GHSA-c978-59m8-c77v), [filelock security fixes](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/security/advisories/GHSA-v4x8-3wr5-3wq8) and [setuptools security fix](https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/security/advisories/GHSA-xmj3-9gf7-h52w).

### Validation

- Python 3.11.14 and Python 3.15.2: **1,876 passed, 10 platform-specific skips on each**, comprising the complete unit suite plus 13 install/lock/pylock integration cases, after the CI dependency-install sequence.
- Python 3.11 with the exact minimum patched versions: **1,863 unit tests and 13 integration tests passed**. The minimum virtualenv also creates, activates and runs pip in Python 3.11/3.15 environments whose paths and prompts contain spaces and apostrophes.
- Fresh `pipenv install --deploy --dev` succeeds using `Pipfile.lock` on Python 3.11 and `pylock.toml` on Python 3.15; `pip check` passes for both.
- All 19 GitHub advisory version ranges are excluded by both lockfiles. Verified hashes for 87 PyPI releases and 903 pylock artifacts, and equivalent package selection for default/dev groups across Linux, Windows and macOS on Python 3.11/3.15.
- `pipenv verify`, all pre-commit hooks (including Ruff/mypy), wheel build and manual build pass. The wheel declares Python >=3.11 and pip rejects it for Python 3.10.

Local execution was on Linux; Windows/macOS runtime verification is covered by the expanded CI matrix. Dependabot alerts can close after this is merged and GitHub rescans the default branch.

title: fix(install): decode requirements.txt like pip when importing with -r
body:
### The issue

`import_requirements` (`pipenv install -r requirements.txt`) reads the file once with `open(r)`, which uses the locale encoding, to find the `-i`, `--extra-index-url` and `--trusted-host` lines, and then lets pip's `parse_requirements` parse the same file. pip decodes it itself (UTF-8/16/32 BOMs, a PEP 263 `# coding:` comment, UTF-8 by default), so the two reads can disagree:

- A file saved as UTF-16 with a BOM, which is what `pip freeze > requirements.txt` produces in Windows PowerShell, fails with `UnicodeDecodeError` before pip is even called.
- A UTF-8 file with a BOM keeps the mark at the start of the first line, so an `-i` or `--extra-index-url` on that line is not recognised and the index is silently dropped.
- A file with a coding comment, or with non-ASCII comments on a machine whose locale encoding isn't UTF-8, is decoded differently from how pip decodes it.

### The fix

Read the file as bytes and decode it with the same helper pip uses for requirements files (`_decode_req_file` in the vendored `req_file.py`), so the index scan and `parse_requirements` see the same text.

### Validation

title: fix(requirements): keep the marker of git/VCS entries
body:
### Description
`requirement_from_lockfile` returned from its VCS branch before it applied the entry's markers, while the file branch and the index branch both keep them. So for a `Pipfile.lock` entry like

```json
"pipenv": {"git": "https://github.com/pypa/pipenv.git", "ref": "abc123", "markers": "sys_platform == 'win32'"}
```

`pipenv requirements` wrote `pipenv @ git+https://github.com/pypa/pipenv.git@abc123` with no marker, and the package got installed on every platform.

### Fix
The direct-reference form (`name @ git+url@ref`) now ends with ` ; <markers>` (PEP 508 asks for a space before `;` after a URL). The editable form (`-e git+...#egg=name`) is unchanged, because pip does not read a marker on an editable line (`parse_req_from_editable` drops it).

When an entry has both `os_markers` and `markers`, the three forms (git, file and index) now write them as one PEP 508 expression, `; (A) and (B)`, instead of `; A; B`, which does not parse.

Install side: `requirement_from_lockfile` also builds `pip_line_specified` in `Lockfile.requirements_list`, which `pipenv sync` passes to pip, so pip now receives the marker on install as well as in `pipenv requirements`. Installs do not change, because the same marker is already evaluated on `install_req`.

### Tests
Three unit tests in `tests/unit/test_dependencies_bridges.py`: a VCS entry keeps its marker (and drops it with `include_markers=False`), an editable VCS entry gets none, and `os_markers` plus `markers` are joined with `and` on the git, file and index forms. The first and the third fail without the change. `test_git_branch_contains_slashes` in `tests/integration/test_lockfile.py` now expects the marker of its git entry.

title: fix(pylock): classify packages by the groups that install them, and requires-python as python_version
body:
### The issue

After `pipenv pylock --generate --dev-groups lint`, installing from the resulting `pylock.toml` goes through `PylockFile.convert_to_pipenv_lockfile()`, which has two problems:

- It decides what is a development package by looking for "dev" or "test" in the marker. A package marked `'lint' in dependency_groups` is therefore put in `default` and installed as a regular dependency. Checking group names at all is also wrong for shared packages: `from_lockfile` folds a package present in both sections into one entry with a marker such as `(python_version < '3.11') or ('lint' in dependency_groups)`, and a name check drops it out of `default`, so a production install misses a runtime dependency.
- `requires-python = ">=3.12"` is copied verbatim into `_meta.requires.python_version`, where Pipfile.lock expects a version such as `3.12`.

### The fix

- Packages are classified by whether they install. Each marker is evaluated with only `default-groups` and with all groups: `default` when it installs with the default groups, `develop` when the marker names a non-default group and it installs with all groups, and both when both hold, as Pipfile.lock repeats shared packages. Packages without a `dependency_groups` clause stay in `default` only.
- `requires-python` is mapped back to the form `from_lockfile` writes: `>=X.Y` becomes `python_version = "X.Y"` and `==X.Y.Z` becomes `python_full_version = "X.Y.Z"`. Any other specifier (for example `>=3.9,<3.13`) is kept as it was.

### Validation

title: fix: replace lockfiles atomically
body:
### The issue

`atomic_open_for_write()` deletes the existing lockfile before renaming the temporary file. If the rename fails, the old `Pipfile.lock` or `pylock.toml` is lost. Concurrent readers can also see a missing file between the two operations.

This is reproducible on Windows without mocking: keep a second read handle open on the temporary file while exiting the context manager. Windows rejects the rename with `PermissionError`, after the original lockfile has already been removed.

The implementation dates back to #2077, whose patch explicitly notes that Python 2 lacked `os.replace()`. Pipenv now requires Python 3.10 or later. There is no separate issue for this follow-up.

### The fix

Replace the closed, same-directory temporary file with `Path.replace()` directly. This supports overwriting on Windows, removes the unlink/rename gap, and preserves the existing lockfile when replacement fails.

Add regression coverage for text/binary writes, new/existing targets, errors during writing and replacement, and both lockfile writers.

title: Read and write the Pipfile as UTF-8 everywhere
body:
### The issue

No issue filed; this is a follow-up to #6750.

`Pipfile.read()` decodes the Pipfile as `utf-8-sig`, but a few other places still open it with the locale encoding: the Pipfile hash (`Pipfile.calculate_hash()`), the lock data built from the Pipfile when there is no usable `Pipfile.lock` (`Lockfile.as_dict()` and `Lockfile.load()` when `_meta` is missing), and `Pipfile.write_toml()`. On Windows the locale encoding is a legacy code page, so a Pipfile with any non-ASCII text, even just a comment, breaks:

- `pipenv lock` on Japanese Windows (cp932) with `# 開発用の依存関係` at the top of the Pipfile:
  ```
  File "...\pipenv\utils\lockfile.py", line 205, in as_dict
  ...
  UnicodeDecodeError: 'cp932' codec can't decode byte 0x82 in position 25: illegal multibyte sequence
  ```
- `pipenv install colorama` with the same Pipfile rewrites it in cp932 (the comment becomes `\x8aJ\x94\xad...`) and then fails with `UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x8a`, because the next read is UTF-8. The Pipfile stays broken for every later command and on every other machine.

Separately, `pipenv.utils.locking.Lockfile.load()` still reads `Pipfile.lock` with the locale encoding. With a BOM, `json` raises `JSONDecodeError`, so the lockfile is reported as corrupt and moved to `Pipfile.lock.bak` (on Linux too).

### The fix

Read the Pipfile as `utf-8-sig` and write it as UTF-8 in those places, and read `Pipfile.lock` as `utf-8-sig` in `locking.Lockfile.load()`, matching what #6750 did for the other readers. A Pipfile that pipenv rewrites still loses its BOM, as before.

`tests/unit/test_pipfile_encoding.py` adds 9 cases (Pipfile with non-ASCII text, saved with and without a BOM, through the hash, `write_toml()`, both Pipfile-derived lock paths, plus a `Pipfile.lock` with a BOM through `locking.Lockfile.load()`). On Windows with cp932 all 9 fail without the change; under UTF-8 (`-X utf8`, like Linux) the 4 BOM cases fail. All pass with it. `tests/unit` otherwise gives the same results as on `main` here (`test_help` and the `test_release_tasks.py`/`test_vendor.py` imports already fail locally).

Aborting makes a malicious or malformed archive visible to the caller instead of yielding a quietly incomplete extraction, and matches the behavior of the standard library's tarfile extraction filters.

Both the tar and zip formats specify / as the only path separator, but the guard against .. components split member names on / alone, so a name such as ..\escaped.txt was treated as a single component and then resolved as a traversal by the filesystem on Windows. title: Read Pipfile, Pipfile.lock, pylock.toml and pyproject.toml saved with a UTF-8 BOM
body:
## The issue

Editors such as Windows Notepad add a UTF-8 BOM when they save a file as UTF-8. pipenv reads its files with `encoding="utf-8"` (or the locale default for the Pipfile), which keeps the BOM as a leading `﻿`. The TOML and JSON parsers reject it, so a Pipfile with a BOM fails with a `TOMLDecodeError` ("Invalid statement (at line 1, column 1)") and a `Pipfile.lock` with a BOM is reported as corrupt (`LockfileCorruptException`).

## The fix

The readers now decode with `utf-8-sig`, which strips a leading BOM and behaves like `utf-8` otherwise:

- `pipenv/utils/pipfile.py`: `Pipfile.read()` (feeds `Pipfile.parsed`) and `ProjectFile.read()`
- `pipenv/utils/pylock.py`: `PylockFile.from_path`, `from_pyproject`, `from_lockfile`
- `pipenv/utils/lockfile.py`: `Lockfile.load`

Writes are unchanged, so a file pipenv rewrites loses the BOM.

## Tests

`tests/unit/test_bom_readers.py`, 6 cases (Pipfile via `Pipfile.parsed` and `ProjectFile.read`, `pylock.toml`, `pyproject.toml`, `Pipfile.lock` via `PylockFile.from_lockfile` and `Lockfile.load`), each writing the file with a BOM. All 6 fail on `main` and pass with the change. `tests/unit`: 1735 passed (without `test_release_tasks.py`, `test_vendor.py` and `test_prefetch.py`, which already fail to import or run in the local test environment on `main`). `ruff check` is clean.

* [x] A news fragment in the `news/` directory to describe this fix with the extension `.bugfix.rst`

title: Add interactive `pipenv init` for creating a Pipfile
body:
Closes #5792

Adds `pipenv init`, which creates a Pipfile through a short dialog, similar to `npm init`:

```
$ pipenv init
Import packages from requirements.txt? [y/n] (y):    # only if one exists
Python version (3.12):
Package index URL (https://pypi.org/simple):
Packages (space-separated, blank for none): requests 'flask[async]>=3'
Dev packages (space-separated, blank for none): pytest
Created …/Pipfile
Create the virtualenv and lock now? [y/n] (y):
```

### Behavior
- `-y/--yes` accepts every default without prompting (like `npm init -y`). It's implied when stdin isn't a TTY, so CI never hangs on a prompt.
- `--install/--no-install` controls whether the virtualenv and lock get created afterwards. By default it asks; under `--yes` it skips. Installing goes through the normal `do_install`.
- `--python` accepts either a bare version (`3.12`) or an interpreter path.
- It won't overwrite an existing Pipfile in the current directory. A Pipfile in a *parent* directory doesn't block it: `Project()` chdirs into the found project's folder at startup, so `init` switches back to the directory it was invoked from.
- Packages in the dialog are parsed as plain PEP 508 requirements (with `shlex`, so quoted markers and `>=3,<4` both work). Paths, URLs and VCS references are rejected with a note to add them later with `pipenv install`, since only the full install code builds correct entries for those.

### Scope
The issue also asked for name/version/author prompts. Those belong in `pyproject.toml`, not a Pipfile, so the dialog only covers what a Pipfile records. The docs say so.

### Testing
- New `tests/unit/test_init_routine.py` (16 tests): requirement parsing, `--yes` with requirements.txt import, bare `--python` version, refusing an existing Pipfile, the parent-Pipfile case, and the full interactive dialog with mocked prompts.
- Pre-commit (ruff, mypy) passes.
- Tested by hand through a pty: the dialog, rejecting a path package, and the parent-Pipfile case. Also ran `pipenv --python 3.12 init -y --install`, which imported a requirements.txt, built the venv and wrote `Pipfile.lock`.

title: Enable mypy type checking for pipenv's own code
body:
Closes #5335.

## What

- Adds a `mirrors-mypy` (v2.4.0) pre-commit hook. CI's lint job already runs `pre-commit run --all-files`, so mypy now gates CI without a workflow change.
- Updates the stale `[tool.mypy]` config. It was targeting Python 3.7, pointing at a `typeshed/` dir that doesn't exist and generating an HTML report that needs lxml. It now targets 3.10, checks `pipenv/`, excludes `pipenv/vendor/` and `pipenv/patched/`, and uses `follow_imports = "skip"` so imports into them aren't followed.
- **Vendored and patched packages are untouched.**
- Fixes all 201 existing errors across pipenv's 77 modules. Most fixes correct annotations or convert legacy `# type:` comments to inline annotations. Ruff doesn't count type comments as using an import, so they caused unused-import errors once the typing names were imported. `# type: ignore` is limited to code that's genuinely dynamic, such as the private `_normalized_name`/`_path` attributes on `importlib.metadata` distributions and the `latest_version` attribute set on them at runtime.

## Small real fixes mypy surfaced

- `get_pip_args` passed a bare `src_dir` string to `list.extend`, which would add one argument per character. It now produces `["--src", src_dir]`. No caller passes it today.
- `Lockfile.from_data` built a `ProjectFile` with a `str` location, which would break `ProjectFile.write()` (`str` has no `.open`). It now passes a `Path`.
- `Environment.is_satisfied` and `safe_import` used pkg_resources APIs (`.location`, `.has_metadata`, `.project_name`, `.activate`) on stdlib distributions. Neither path can actually run, so this isn't a user-facing fix. In `is_satisfied`, the earlier `req.specifier` check always returns first. The `safe_import` fallback runs only when `_modules[name]` is falsy, which never happens. I switched the first to the importlib equivalents and removed the second.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

Mypy still skips the bodies of functions with no annotations. Turning on `check_untyped_defs` to check them is the natural next step, best done one module at a time.

## Testing

- `mypy`: no issues in 77 source files
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: all hooks pass
- Unit: 1760 passed, 10 skipped
- Integration: 250 passed. 15 failed locally, and the same 15 fail on `main` in this environment (local mirror/index fixtures), so this branch doesn't cause them.

title: Skip "*" versions when pinning resolved default deps as constraints
body:
### The issue

Since 2026.4.0, `pipenv lock` fails for a Pipfile that has a default package whose markers exclude the current platform, if the Pipfile also has `[dev-packages]`:

```toml
[packages]
requests = "*"
colorama = {version = "*", markers = "sys_platform == 'win32'"}

[dev-packages]
pytest = "*"
```

```
$ pipenv lock          # on Linux, pipenv 2026.10.0 / main
pipenv.exceptions.ResolutionFailure: ERROR: ERROR: Invalid requirement:
'colorama*': Expected semicolon (after name with no version specifier) or end
    colorama*
            ^ (from line 2 of /tmp/pipenv-...-requirements/pipenv-...-constraints.txt)
```

title: Write one pylock.toml entry for packages locked in both default and develop
body:
### The issue

`Pipfile.lock` repeats a dependency that both package categories need in `default` and in `develop`. For example, `packaging` is required by an app dependency and by `pytest`. `PylockFile.from_lockfile` writes one `[[packages]]` entry per section:

```toml
[[packages]]
name = "packaging"
version = "26.3"
marker = "python_version >= '3.9'"

[[packages]]
name = "packaging"
version = "26.3"
marker = "('dev' in dependency_groups) and (python_version >= '3.9')"
```

With the dev group selected, both entries match. [PEP 751](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/pylock-toml/#packages) requires every install to narrow down to a single entry per package, so the generated file can't be installed with the dev group:

```
$ pipenv lock && pipenv pylock --generate      # Pipfile: [packages] packaging, requests / [dev-packages] pytest
$ uv pip install -r pylock.toml --group dev
error: Multiple active package entries found for `packaging`

$ rm Pipfile.lock && pipenv sync --dev          # pylock.toml only
Error loading pylock.toml: Package 'packaging' has 2 entries that match the
environment; they must narrow down to a single entry
$ .venv/bin/python -c "import pytest"
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pytest'
```

When `Pipfile.lock` is still present, `pipenv sync --dev` prints the same error and falls back to `Pipfile.lock`. Without it, the dev packages aren't installed. Installs without the dev group aren't affected.

### The fix

When a develop package pins the same artifact as its default copy (identical `Pipfile.lock` entries apart from `markers`), `from_lockfile` now keeps only the default entry:

- If the default entry has no marker, or the same marker as the develop copy, it already applies whenever the develop one would. It's kept unchanged.
- If the markers differ, the default marker is widened to `(<default marker>) or (<dev group marker> and <develop marker>)`. The single entry then covers both installs.

If the two copies differ in anything else (version, source, hashes), both entries are kept as before.

This changes the export side only. The read-side narrowing added in #6734 is unchanged, and it now finds a single matching entry for such packages.

I considered keeping two entries and making them mutually exclusive (adding `not ('dev' in dependency_groups)` to the default one). That would make the default entry depend on the group selection and drop the package from installs that select the dev group, so a single widened entry is simpler and matches what the lock means.

### Testing

- New `test_from_lockfile_package_in_default_and_develop_has_one_entry` covers 4 marker combinations: none/none, equal, default-only, and both different. It checks there's a single entry, its marker, and that `_narrow_package_entries()` returns one `packaging`. All 4 cases fail before the change.
- `pytest tests/unit`: 1747 passed (base 1743 plus the 4 new). `test_release_tasks.py` and `test_vendor.py` fail to import in both runs because the release and vendoring tools aren't installed.
- `ruff check` on the changed files: clean.

title: Keep non-group conditions of pylock.toml markers that name a dependency group
body:
### The issue

When pipenv installs from a `pylock.toml`, `Lockfile._pip_marker` strips the PEP 751 `dependency_groups` conditions before handing markers to pip. It only recognises the shape pipenv writes itself, `('dev' in dependency_groups) and (<marker>)`. Any other marker that mentions `dependency_groups` is dropped entirely, together with its platform or Python version conditions.

`pdm export -f pylock` writes markers in a different shape:

```toml
[[packages]]
name = "colorama"
marker = "sys_platform == \"win32\" and \"dev\" in dependency_groups"

[[packages]]
name = "tomli"
marker = "python_version < \"3.11\" and \"dev\" in dependency_groups"
```

End to end on Linux with Python 3.14: a project whose dev group has `colorama; sys_platform == 'win32'` and `tomli; python_version < '3.11'`, a `pylock.toml` from `pdm export -f pylock`, no `Pipfile.lock`, then `pipenv sync --dev`:

- `main`: installs `six`, `colorama` and `tomli`. Both markers were dropped.
- this branch: installs `six` only.

### The fix

`pipenv/utils/locking.py`: `_pip_marker` now parses the marker with the vendored `packaging` and treats every `'<group>' in dependency_groups` condition as true, since pipenv has already selected the group. In an `and` the condition is dropped. If an `or` branch is left with only group conditions, the whole marker is true and no marker is passed. The rest is kept as is. Markers without `dependency_groups` are returned unchanged, as before. The shapes pipenv writes itself give the same result as before.

### Validation

- New `tests/unit/test_pylock_group_markers.py`: 8 cases covering pipenv's own shapes, pdm's shapes, a group `or` inside parentheses, a three-term `and`, and a marker without groups. The 4 non-pipenv shapes fail on `main`.

title: Brace bare $VAR in source URLs for pipenv requirements --no-lock

### The issue

pip only expands environment variables written as `${VAR}` in a requirements file. Since #5272, `pipenv requirements` writes a bare `$VAR` in a lockfile source URL as `${VAR}` for that reason. title: Fix fabricated artifact entries in generated pylock.toml
body:
### The issue

Fixes #6738. Converting `Pipfile.lock` to `pylock.toml` currently invents `py3-none-any` wheel filenames and constructs file URLs under `/simple/`. The filenames can have the wrong tags, hashes can belong to sdists, and the URLs return 404.

### The fix

Look up each indexed package in its Simple API index and match its locked SHA-256 hashes to actual distribution files. Write the real wheel and sdist names, URLs, and corresponding hashes. If a hash cannot be matched, do not create a file entry for it; retain it under `packages.tool.pipenv` so Pipenv can round-trip the lock without losing its hash checks. An unmatched package may still lack enough file information for another installer to install it.

Add offline regression coverage for JSON and HTML Simple API responses, hash matching, URL credential removal, and unknown hashes.

title: Keep local, VCS and file sources in pylock.toml
body:
### The issue

With `use_pylock = true`, dependencies that don't come from the index lose their source in `pylock.toml`, and installing from it looks the name up on the index instead:

- **Writing** (`PylockFile.from_lockfile`): a Pipfile.lock entry like `{"path": "./localpkg"}`, `{"editable": true, "path": ...}`, `{"git": ..., "ref": ...}` or `{"file": "https://.../pkg.tar.gz"}` becomes `name` + `index = "https://pypi.org/simple/"` (plus fabricated `wheels` when it has hashes). The path/VCS/URL is dropped.
- **Reading** (`convert_to_pipenv_lockfile`): PEP 751 `directory`, `vcs` and `archive` packages, e.g. from another tool, become `{"version": "==0.1.0"}` or `{"version": "*"}` index pins.

End to end, with `localpkg-d5 = {path = "./localpkg"}` in the Pipfile: `pipenv lock` writes `[[packages]] name = "localpkg-d5"` with `index = "https://pypi.org/simple/"` and no path. `pipenv sync` from that `pylock.toml` then fails with `No matching distribution found for localpkg-d5`. If a package with the same name exists on the index, that package gets installed instead of the local one.

### The fix

In `pipenv/utils/pylock.py`:

- Writing: path, editable, VCS (`git`/`hg`/`svn`/`bzr`) and file entries become PEP 751 `packages.directory` (`path`, `editable`, `subdirectory`), `packages.vcs` (`type`, `url`, `commit-id` from `ref`, `subdirectory`) and `packages.archive` (`url` or `path`, `hashes`). They get no `index` or `wheels`. A `path` to a file with an archive suffix (`.whl`, `.tar.gz`, `.zip`...) is an `archive`.
- Reading: the reverse mapping, and these entries get no `version` pin. PEP 751 writes relative paths as `localpkg`, which pipenv reads as a package name, so a bare relative path gets a leading `./`.

### Validation

- New `tests/unit/test_pylock_sources.py` (6 tests): the four entry kinds are written as `directory`/`vcs`/`archive` without `index`/`wheels`, each one round-trips back to the same Pipfile.lock entry without a version, and a `directory` package written by another tool converts to `{"path": "./localpkg"}`. All fail on `main`.
- `tests/unit`: 1708 passed. The 2 failures and 2 errors in `test_prefetch.py`, `test_release_tasks.py` and `test_vendor.py` happen on `main` too in this environment. `tests/integration/test_pylock.py`: 5 passed. `ruff check` (0.9.3) is clean.
- End to end, a Pipfile with a local path dependency → `pipenv lock` → `pipenv sync` from `pylock.toml` only, and a hand-written `pylock.toml` with `directory = { path = "localpkg" }`:
  - `main`: the path is missing from `pylock.toml` and `sync` fails (`No matching distribution found`).
  - this branch: `pylock.toml` has `[packages.directory] path = "./localpkg"`, and both syncs install the local package.

Not in this PR: index packages still get `wheels` entries built from the Pipfile.lock hashes with made-up file names and URLs (`https://pypi.org/simple/<name>/<name>-<version>-py3-none-any.whl`, one per hash, including the sdist's). Other PEP 751 installers fail on them (`uv pip install -r pylock.toml` returns a 404). Fixing that needs the real file names from the index, so it's a separate change.

title: Accept a newer minor pylock.toml lock-version with a warning
body:
### The issue

[PEP 751](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/pylock-toml/#lock-version) says of `lock-version`: "If a tool supports the major version but not the minor version, a tool SHOULD warn when an unknown key is seen. If a tool doesn't support a major version, it MUST raise an error." The Installation section repeats it: "an error or warning MUST be raised as appropriate".

`PylockFile.from_path()` raises `PylockVersionError` for anything but `"1.0"`, so a `lock-version = "1.1"` lock is rejected. That error is caught while the lock is loaded, so the failure is quiet. With a `pylock.toml` (`lock-version = "1.1"`, one package `six`) and a Pipfile with no packages, `pipenv sync` on `main`:

```
Error loading pylock.toml: Unsupported lock-version: 1.1. Only version 1.0 is supported.
Installing dependencies from Pipfile.lock (3cbc06)...
All dependencies are now up-to-date!
```

It writes an empty `Pipfile.lock` from the Pipfile, installs nothing and exits 0.

### The fix

`from_path()` parses `lock-version` as `major.minor`:
- major other than 1: `PylockVersionError` as before ("Unsupported lock-version");
- not `<int>.<int>`: `PylockVersionError` ("Invalid lock-version");
- 1.x with x > 0: the file loads, and pipenv warns once per file that keys added after 1.0 are ignored. The lock is read several times per command, hence the once-per-file guard.

A per-key warning would need the list of keys each version defines; the single warning covers the same case without that.

### Validation

- `tests/unit/test_pylock_lock_version.py`: 1.1 loads with one warning across two loads, 1.0 loads with no warning, and 2.0, 0.9, `1`, `one.0` raise. `tests/unit`: 1695 passed. title: Pick the matching entry for packages listed more than once in pylock.toml
body:
### The issue

PEP 751 lets a `pylock.toml` list a package more than once with different markers, e.g. one version per Python range, which `uv` writes for universal locks. The [Installation section](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/pylock-toml/#installation) skips entries whose marker doesn't match, and requires the remaining ones to narrow down to a single entry ("an error about the ambiguity MUST be raised otherwise").

`convert_to_pipenv_lockfile()` writes one Pipfile.lock entry per name, so the last entry for a name overwrote the earlier ones. When that last entry's marker excluded the target Python, the package wasn't installed at all and `pipenv sync` still exited 0:

```toml
[[packages]]
name = "six"
version = "1.16.0"
marker = "python_version >= '3.12'"
# wheels…

[[packages]]
name = "six"
version = "1.17.0"
marker = "python_version < '3.12'"
# wheels…
```

`pipenv sync --python 3.12` on `main`: `Ignoring six: markers <Marker('python_version < "3.12"')> don't match your environment`, exit 0, `six` not installed. Swap the two entries and 1.16.0 is installed.

### The fix

- `PylockFile._narrow_package_entries()` groups entries by name. For a name listed more than once, it keeps the entry whose marker matches the environment, raises `PylockFormatError` if more than one matches, and keeps the first entry if none matches (the install step then skips it as it does for a single excluded entry). Order follows each name's first entry.
- `convert_to_pipenv_lockfile()` takes an optional `environment`, and `Lockfile` passes the target virtualenv's marker variables from `_target_marker_environment()` (#6647), so the entry is picked for the virtualenv's Python and not the interpreter running pipenv. Without a virtualenv (or with `--system`) it falls back to the running interpreter.
- Markers are evaluated with all extras and dependency groups in the lock, since this only decides between entries of the same name. Group and extra filtering stays where it is.

The import of `_target_marker_environment` in `lockfile.py` is lazy because `pipenv.routines.install` imports that module.

### Validation

- `tests/unit/test_pylock_duplicate_entries.py`: picks the right entry for both Python ranges in both orders, keeps an excluded entry when none matches, raises when two entries match, and keeps the order of first entries. They fail on `main`.
- `tests/unit`: 1696 passed. The 2 failures and 2 errors in `test_prefetch.py`, `test_release_tasks.py` and `test_vendor.py` also happen on `main` in my environment.
- End to end with the lock above, pipenv on Python 3.14 and `pipenv sync --python 3.12`: `six` 1.16.0 is installed in both orders.

title: Check pylock.toml requires-python and environments before installing
body:
### The issue

Fixes #6732. `pipenv sync` from a `pylock.toml` installed locks that don't apply to the target Python, with exit 0 and no warning. The [pylock spec's Installation section](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/pylock-toml/#installation) requires an error when the top-level `requires-python`, the `environments` list, or the `requires-python` of a package that would be installed excludes the environment.

### The fix

- `PylockFile.check_environment()` (`pipenv/utils/pylock.py`) checks the three cases and raises `PylockEnvironmentError`. Packages are selected with `get_packages_for_environment()`, so a package excluded by its marker (e.g. `tomli` with `python_version < '3.11'`) isn't checked. `get_packages_for_environment()` gains an `environment` argument for that.
- `do_install_dependencies()` runs the check before installing whenever it installs from `pylock.toml`, against the target virtualenv's Python. It uses `_target_marker_environment()` (from #6647), so `pipenv sync --python 3.10` run by a newer interpreter checks 3.10. The error is a `PipenvException`, so it prints without a traceback:

  ```
  ERROR: /path/pylock.toml can't be installed: Python 3.12.3 does not satisfy the
  requires-python '>=3.13' of package 'six'
  ```

- Dependency groups: the default groups are checked, plus every group in the lock when dev packages are installed, which is how the converter already sorts dev packages. Extras aren't filtered by the converter, so all of them are included.

The check is in the install routine instead of `convert_to_pipenv_lockfile()` because `Lockfile.as_dict()` catches conversion errors and falls back to the Pipfile.

### Validation

- 8 new tests in `tests/unit/test_pylock.py`: the three cases from the issue, a matching lock, a package skipped by its marker, dependency group selection, an invalid `requires-python`, and the error raised from the install routine. `tests/unit`: 1697 passed. Summary

Migrates pipenv's tests/integration/test_*.py suite (29 files) off a dependency on real network access / pypi.org, so the full integration suite can run under --network=none / unshare --net — and, along the way, fixes four real pipenv bugs the migration surfaced.

Mechanism: a file:// PEP 503 "simple" package index built from the existing tests/pypi submodule plus a small set of new minimal stub/vendored wheels under tests/test_artifacts/extra_pypi/. Zero sockets involved — pip's own file:// index support (_internal/index/collector.py) handles it natively. VCS tests use git+file:// against throwaway local git repos built on the fly, for the same reason.

Scope:
- 29 test files migrated, each its own commit, to a new pipenv_instance_file_pypi fixture that coexists with the old pipenv_instance_pypi/pipenv_instance_private_pypi fixtures (not a replacement — nothing else in the test suite was touched).
- 4 product-code bug fixes (pipenv/utils/internet.py, sources.py, dependencies.py, constants.py, routines/install.py), ~99 lines changed total.
- 2 fixture/golden-file-only fixes (no product code).

Impact

- Test suite can now run fully offline. Previously every integration test either hit real pypi.org or a local pypiserver subprocess bound to loopback; neither works under --network=none. This was the actual motivation for the whole change.
- Four real pipenv bugs fixed, independent of the test migration itself:
  a. --pypi-mirror/--index/a requirements.txt -i <url> line all silently failed or crashed for file:// URLs (is_valid_url() rejected them; the resulting exception was swallowed with no visible error). Anyone using a local/offline package index with these flags was affected.
  b. A file=...+extras=[...] Pipfile dependency crashed pip's archive-type detection with a raw FileNotFoundError for any file:// source — a plain misleading crash, not just an offline-specific issue.
  c. A VCS dependency (git+...) whose package name also exists in the configured index got silently collapsed from {git=..., ref=...} down to a bare version-string requirement — this reproduces for any git+file:// dependency, not just offline tests, and would have silently rewritten a real Pipfile incorrectly on pipenv install/update.
  d. Not a product bug — a resolver-protocol smoke test had stale golden fixtures; regenerated.
- Net new test coverage: none removed, several tests that previously only exercised real-network paths now also get an offline-equivalent run.

Risk

- Size: 78 files changed — mechanical and repetitive (each test file's diff is "swap fixture, add [[source]] where needed"), but large enough that a line-by-line human review of every file is impractical; recommend spot-checking a handful plus the product-code diff closely.
- Product-code bug fixes carry real behavior-change risk, despite being small:
  - import_requirements() now replaces the Pipfile's auto-created default pypi.org source with a -i <url> directive's index, rather than adding a second source alongside it — this changes Pipfile output for anyone currently relying on the (arguably already-broken) old two-source behavior from a bare requirements.txt conversion.
  - VCS_SCHEMES gaining git+file/hg+file/svn+file/bzr+file changes write-back behavior for any existing Pipfile with a file://-scheme VCS dependency — previously-collapsed entries will now be preserved correctly, which is a visible diff for existing users relying on (knowingly or not) the old behavior.
  - None of the four fixes have been run against pipenv's full existing test suite in CI — only a local run (1678 unit tests, full integration suite under a dead-proxy offline check) in this environment. No CI signal yet.
- New binary artifacts: 35 new vendored wheel files under tests/test_artifacts/extra_pypi/ (all small, a few KB–30KB; two are real upstream wheels — pysocks==1.7.1, cerberus==1.3.8 — the rest are synthetic metadata-only stubs). Worth a glance to confirm nothing unexpected snuck in.
- Known residual risk, not fixed, flagged in-repo (tests/integration/KNOWN_ISSUES_offline_migration.md — currently missing from the working tree; see note below): an unconstrained */range pin on a package name that also has a metadata-only stub in extra_pypi can silently resolve to the stub instead of the real vendored package as extra_pypi grows (already happened once, masking a Python-3.12 incompatibility one test was meant to catch — not fixed, out of scope).

Testing

- Full unit test suite: 1678 passed, 11 skipped (Windows-only), 2 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change (missing requests module in the local verification venv).
- Full integration suite re-run under a dead-proxy environment variable (HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:1 etc.) to prove no real network call succeeds silently — any accidental real-network dependency fails loudly instead of passing by accident.
- Each of the four bug fixes verified independently via a minimal hand-built repro before being wired into its corresponding test.

title: Fix resolver_backend precedence and pure-python lock failures; benchmark both backends
body:
## Summary

**Bug fix: `[pipenv] resolver_backend` was ignored by `update` / `upgrade` / `uninstall`.**
`pipenv lock` reads the documented `resolver_backend` key itself, but every other caller of `venv_resolve_deps` passes only the CLI `--backend` value. The fallback in `_selected_backend_for_request` checked `PIPENV_RESOLVER` and the legacy `[pipenv] resolver` alias, never `resolver_backend`. So a project that opted into the pure-Python backend in v2026.9.0 silently re-locked with pip on `pipenv update`, `pipenv upgrade` and `pipenv uninstall`.

The fix makes `_selected_backend_for_request` prefer `resolver_backend` over `resolver`, matching `do_lock` and the subprocess-side fallback in `pipenv/resolver/core.py`. Because the selected backend also feeds the resolution cache key, a Pipfile-selected backend can no longer be served a pip-resolved cache entry.

**CI benchmark now covers both backends.**
- `benchmarks/benchmark.py` gains `--backend {pip,pure-python}`. It selects the backend through `[pipenv] resolver_backend` in the benchmark Pipfile, so `lock`, `update` and `add-package` all go through the same path users take. The default `pip` run leaves the key unset so its numbers stay comparable with earlier runs.
- The `benchmark` CI job is now a matrix over `pip` and `pure-python`, with one step-summary table and one `pipenv-benchmark-stats-<backend>` artifact per backend. The `pure-python` job is `continue-on-error` while the backend is experimental.
- `stats.csv` and `benchmark-results.json` label non-default backends (`pipenv (pure-python)` and a `backend` field).

**Pure-python fixes surfaced by the new benchmark job.** The first `pure-python` benchmark run failed, which uncovered two real problems:

1. *sdist hash check crashed on every PyPI sdist* (`pure_python_sdist.py`). The SHA-256 check treated `candidate.hashes` as a `{"sha256": [...]}` dict, but candidates carry a `frozenset[Hash]`. Any sdist built for metadata from an index that publishes hashes (all of PyPI) failed with `AttributeError: 'frozenset' object has no attribute 'get'`. No test covered a candidate with hashes; I added matching and mismatching cases.
2. *Lock of the Sentry set never finished* (`pure_python_provider.py`). One parent requires `protobuf>=5.27.3,<6` while about ten require `>=6.33.5,<8`. While backtracking out of that, resolvelib repeated the same unsatisfiable `find_matches("protobuf")` query thousands of times. Each call re-read and re-parsed the on-disk manifest and filtered ~2,900 protobuf files twice. Fixed by:
   - keeping parsed manifests in memory per resolve, and
   - memoizing `find_matches` on every input the filters read (identifier, each requirement's specifier and prerelease opt-in, rejected set), as pip does with `lru_cache` on `PackageFinder.find_best_candidate`.

   Locally the Sentry resolve went from not finishing after 10+ minutes to about 10s with a warm cache, and produced an identical 149-package lock.

Note: the pip benchmark artifact name changed from `pipenv-benchmark-stats` to `pipenv-benchmark-stats-pip`. Nothing in the repo consumes it.

## Verification
- Four new unit tests in `tests/unit/test_resolver_parent_dispatch.py`. Three of them fail on `main` and pass with the fix; the fourth pins that the CLI value and `PIPENV_RESOLVER` still win over the Pipfile.
- End-to-end check: on a project with `resolver_backend = "pure-python"`, `pipenv upgrade six` dispatched to `pip` on `main` and to `pure-python` on this branch.
- Confirmed that `pipenv install -r requirements.txt` (the benchmark import step) keeps the `[pipenv]` section when it rewrites the Pipfile.
- 5 new provider tests and 2 new sdist tests; the sdist tests fail without the fix.
- `tests/unit`: 1692 passed, 10 skipped. pre-commit is clean.

title: Fix `pipenv requirements` mirror selection (pypi_mirror not used in export)

Fix `pipenv requirements` mirror selection (pypi_mirror not used in export)

`pipenv requirements` ignored an explicitly selected PyPI mirror
(`--pypi-mirror` flag / `PIPENV_PYPI_MIRROR` env var) in both export
paths, always emitting index URLs from the Pipfile/lockfile sources.
The mirror options exist for other commands but were never wired into
the requirements routine, so users behind mirrors (e.g. corporate or
regional PyPI mirrors) could not export requirements pointing at them.

This threads the existing `pypi_mirror` state into
`generate_requirements()` and applies the existing
`create_mirror_source()` / `replace_pypi_sources()` helpers to the
sources in both the locked and `--no-lock` paths. Private indexes are
preserved, and neither the Pipfile nor the lockfile is modified.

Fixes #5270

Tests: new `tests/unit/test_requirements_mirror.py` exercises both
export paths across flag/env/precedence/default/exclude-index
selections via real subprocess CLI runs (10 cases, red before the fix:
8 failed, green after: 10 passed). Full `tests/unit` suite: 1670 passed
before, 1680 passed after, 0 failures both sides.

title: fix(markers): stop collapsing python_version exclusions into `not in`
body:
Fixes #6727

## Problem

`Requires-Python` exclusions such as colorama 0.4.6's `!=3.0.*, !=3.1.*, …, !=3.6.*, >=2.7` were collapsed into `python_version not in '3.0, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6'`. Marker `in` / `not in` use string containment, so `'3.1' in '3.10, 3.11'` is true. The packaging spec now explicitly disallows this for version fields (pypa/packaging.python.org#1988). The collapsed marker ended up in `Pipfile.lock` and in `pipenv requirements` output.

## Changes (`pipenv/utils/markers.py`)

- `cleanup_pyspecs` now emits one `python_version != 'X'` clause per excluded version.
- Several `==` versions are written as a parenthesized `or` of `==` clauses instead of `in '…'`.
- Clauses are ordered by version rather than as strings, so `3.9` comes before `3.10`.
- Fixed parsing of existing `python_version not in …` markers, e.g. from older lockfiles. A missing-space format string built `python_versionnot in"…"`, which raised `InvalidMarker`. Those markers are now read correctly and rewritten in the new form.

colorama 0.4.6 now gives:

```
python_version >= "2.7" and python_version != "3.0" and python_version != "3.1" and python_version != "3.2" and python_version != "3.3" and python_version != "3.4" and python_version != "3.5" and python_version != "3.6"
```

## Tests

- New `tests/unit/test_markers.py`. It checks the marker text and also evaluates the markers, so 3.10 and 3.11 must be allowed and 3.1 excluded.
- Unit suite: 1670 passed.
- Marker integration tests: 18 passed. `test_global_overrides_environment_markers` and `test_platform_python_implementation_marker` fail the same way on `main` in my local environment, because the local test package server wasn't running.

title: feat(sync): add --clean to uninstall packages missing from the lock
body:
## Summary

Implements step 1 of #6724: an opt-in `pipenv sync --clean`, equivalent to `pipenv sync && pipenv clean`.

- The removal logic in `pipenv/routines/clean.py` is split out of `do_clean` into `remove_extraneous_packages()` so `sync` can reuse it without `sys.exit`
- The flag travels through `RoutineContext` (`InstallPolicy.clean`), keeping `do_sync(project, ctx)` unchanged
- Like `pipenv clean`, packages locked in **any** category are kept; the `--dev`/`--categories` selection only affects what gets installed
- `--clean` is refused with `--system`, so it can't strip unrelated packages from a system interpreter
- Exits non-zero if any uninstall fails
- Small fix: `pipenv clean --bare` was parsed but never passed to `do_clean`; it's now honoured

Steps 2–3 of the proposal (deprecation warning, then flipping the default) are intentionally not included; `sync`'s default behaviour is unchanged.

## Tests

- Unit: `TestDoSyncClean` in `tests/unit/test_lock_sync_uninstall_context_routing.py` (default off, runs after install, failure exit code, refused with `--system`)
- Integration: `test_pipenv_sync_clean` in `tests/integration/test_cli.py`

body:
Bumps the pip group with 1 update in the /examples directory: [urllib3](https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3). Updates `urllib3` from 2.7.0 to 2.8.0
Release notes

Sourced from urllib3's releases.

2.8.0

🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support

urllib3 is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure long-term sustainable maintenance of the project. If your company or organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and maintained for the long-haul.

Thank you for your support.

Security

Fixed the following security issues:

  • The TLS configuration for HTTPS proxies could be ignored or overridden. (High severity, GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77)
  • HTTPResponse.stream() and read_chunked() could buffer a chunk-size line of unbounded length in memory. (High severity, GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw)
  • Chunked Deflate streaming could enter an infinite loop. (Medium severity, GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g)

[!IMPORTANT] urllib3 2.8.0 fixes HTTPS proxy TLS configuration being ignored or overridden by destination settings. Configurations relying on that behavior may require changes.

Configure proxy CA certificates and client certificates in proxy_ssl_context, and proxy identity checks with proxy_assert_hostname or proxy_assert_fingerprint. Destination client certificates and identity overrides no longer apply to HTTPS forwarding proxy connections.

[!NOTE] CVE IDs had not yet been assigned to these advisories at the time of release due to a backlog at GitHub's CNA.

Deprecations & Removals

  • Deprecated using an empty collection as the Retry option allowed_methods to retry any verb. (#5044)

Features

  • Added Url.auth_decoded and Url.auth_decoded_joined convenience properties to the result of parse_url(). (#4945)
  • Added basic_auth_encoding and proxy_basic_auth_encoding parameters to urllib3.util.make_headers(). (#5092)

Bugfixes

  • Fixed response header handling to replace obsolete folded header lines (obs-fold) with spaces in accordance with RFC 9112, preventing raw CRLF sequences from appearing in header values such as Set-Cookie. (#1362)

  • Fixed usage of proxy_ssl_context with ProxyManager when use_forwarding_for_https=True. Passing ssl_context instead of proxy_ssl_context for HTTPS proxies in this configuration now emits a FutureWarning and will raise an error in v3.0. (#2577)

  • Changed behavior of the default ConnectionPool.pool initialization. LifoQueue is now resolved from the queue module after the ConnectionPool is instantiated instead of using the default cached QueueCls class property. This is done because sometimes the queue.LifoQueue is monkey-patched late in the program, such as by gevent. (#3289)

  • Raised UnrewindableBodyError instead of ValueError when retrying a request whose body had tell() but not seek(). (#3779)

  • Decoded percent-encoded SOCKS proxy credentials before authenticating with the proxy server. (#3785)

  • Fixed HTTPResponse.drain_conn() to discard unread response data in 64 KiB chunks (same as the default amt when doing HTTPResponse.stream(...)). (#5019)

  • Fixed is_ipaddress() to detect non-standard IPv4 forms accepted by socket.connect, such as hex (0x7f000001), octal (0177.0.0.1), and decimal integers (2130706433), ensuring SSL certificate verification uses the correct mode for these addresses. (#5029)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen raising a misleading FullPoolError instead of ValueError when called with an invalid timeout argument on a pool created with block=True. (#5059)

  • Fixed port-zero handling to preserve explicit :0 values instead of substituting the default ports 80 or 443 in URL parsing, pool selection, proxy configuration, connection_from_url(), and HTTP/2 request authority. (#5071, #5101)

  • Fixed a bug where PoolManager passed the assert_hostname and assert_fingerprint parameters to HTTP connection pools. (#5077)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen() and HTTP proxy forwarding to strip URL fragments from absolute request targets before sending requests. (#5079)

  • Added safeguards to the proxy tunneling code to prevent potential security issues when handling invalid characters in the proxy host and HTTP headers. This change affects users of Python 3.10, Python 3.11, and Python 3.12 when the standard library does not contain the fix; those on newer Python versions should upgrade to 3.13.14+ or 3.14.5+ to get the same security fixes. (#5091)

  • Fixed HTTPSConnection.connect() overriding ProxyConfig.ssl_context's certificate policy and proxy identity checks with the target connection's TLS settings when forwarding through an HTTPS proxy.

    HTTPSConnection no longer applies target SNI, assertions, or client credentials to forwarding proxy handshakes and continues to use its ssl_context as a fallback when an HTTPS proxy forwards an HTTP target. (#5093)

  • Fixed URL parsing to more strictly enforce RFC 3986 host syntax, rejecting invalid host input such as raw spaces and control characters, malformed percent-encodings, and percent-encoded control characters in HTTP(S) hosts and IPv6 zone identifiers, including proxy CONNECT tunnel targets. Host normalization now also follows RFC 3986 normalization rules for percent-encoded octets by decoding percent-encoded unreserved characters and uppercasing the hexadecimal digits of retained percent-encoded octets. (#5095)

### The issue

Three recent reports expose related reliability and guidance problems:

- the lock-time PyPI hash session does not use pip's combined certificate trust context, so a custom `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` can discard public roots (#6711)

- add focused regression coverage and one Towncrier fragment per issue

title: docs: the documented Python floor is 3.7, pyproject requires 3.10
body:
`pyproject.toml` declares `requires-python = ">=3.10"`, so `pip install pipenv` refuses on 3.7, 3.8 and 3.9. Two documents still tell those readers they are supported.

```
README.md:75             **Pipenv can be installed with Python 3.7 and above.**
docs/installation.md:393 Pipenv requires Python 3.7 or newer.
```

The second one sits under a heading called **Python Version Compatibility**, which is the first place someone checks after a failed install.

## Deliberately not changed

There are other `3.7`/`3.8`/`3.9` mentions in the docs and they are a **different claim**, so this PR leaves them alone:

- `pipenv --python 3.7` in `README.md`, and `pipenv --python 3.8` / `3.9` in `docs/best_practices.md`. These are the interpreter pipenv **provisions for a project**, which is independent of the interpreter pipenv itself runs on. They still work.
- `python_version = "3.9"` in `docs/pipfile.md`, which is the same thing, a Pipfile target.
- `docs/installation.md:39`, "Install pipx (requires Python 3.7+)" states **pipx's** requirement, not pipenv's.

Only the two lines whose subject is pipenv's own installability are touched.

Found with [docproof](https://github.com/melbinjp/docproof), which checks documentation claims against a project's own metadata. It judges a Python-requirement sentence only when the project's own distribution name is the subject standing alone, which is exactly the rule that separates the two lines changed here from the ones left alone.

## Summary

title: Accept a major-only python_version such as "3"
body:
## Summary

Fixes #6687. `python_version = "3"` in the Pipfile `[requires]` section — which [the docs list as valid](https://pipenv.pypa.io/en/latest/specifiers.html#python-version-vs-full-version) — produced a spurious mismatch warning on install and a fatal `DeployException` under `--deploy`.

`_python_version_matches_required` branches on how many components the requirement has, but only distinguished "3 or more" from "everything else":

```python
if len(required_ver_str.split(".")) >= 3:
    return actual == required            # full version, exact
else:
    return actual.major == required.major and actual.minor == required.minor
```

`"3"` has one component, so it took the second branch — and `parse_version("3")` fills in a **zero minor**, so the comparison became `actual.minor == 0`. Every 3.x interpreter except 3.0 was rejected:

```
parse_version("3") -> 3 | major 3 | minor 0
actual=3.13.14  required='3'  -> False
```

## Change

Compare only the components actually given:

| requirement | compared |
| --- | --- |
| `"3"` | major only |
| `"3.13"` | major + minor |
| `"3.13.1"` | exact |

The PEP 440 specifier path (`">=3.9"`, `">=3.9,<4"`) is untouched.

## Tests

`TestPythonVersionMatchesRequired` already has a parametrized table, so the major-only cases go in alongside the existing #6514 substring-regression rows: `3.13.14`/`3.9.1`/`3.0.0`/`3.11` all satisfy `"3"`, while `2.7.18` and `4.0.0` don't, plus `2.7.18` against `"2"` so the rule isn't special-cased to Python 3.

Reverting only `pipenv/` fails exactly the new rows and nothing else:

```
FAILED ...test_version_match[3.13.14-3-True]
FAILED ...test_version_match[3.9.1-3-True]
FAILED ...test_version_match[3.11-3-True]
FAILED ...test_version_match[2.7.18-2-True]
4 failed, 22 passed
```

## Verification

- `pytest tests/unit/test_utils.py -k PythonVersionMatchesRequired` → 26 passed
- `pytest tests/unit/test_utils.py` → **210 passed, 5 skipped** (skips are POSIX-only path tests, I'm on Windows)
- `ruff check` on both changed files → all checks passed
- Added `news/6687.bugfix.rst`

One note: `ruff format --check` reports both changed files as needing reformatting, but that's **pre-existing on a clean tree** (verified by stashing), so I left it alone rather than mixing unrelated reformatting into this diff.

fix(auth): write PIPENV_PYPI_MIRROR credentials to resolver netrc (#6677)
body:
## Problem

Fixes #6677. Since v2026.6.0, `pipenv install` fails with `ResolutionFailure: No matching distribution found` when a private index is configured via `PIPENV_PYPI_MIRROR` with embedded credentials (e.g. `https://user:pass@mirror.example.com`). The credentials are silently dropped and the index returns `401 Unauthorized`.

## Root cause

v2026.6.0 shipped the GHSA-8xgg-v3jj-95m2 fix, which stopped placing index credentials on pip's argv (visible via `ps`/`/proc/<pid>/cmdline`) and instead writes them to a temporary netrc that pip reads.

The regression is an asymmetry in how `PIPENV_PYPI_MIRROR` is applied:

- The **resolver subprocess** (`pipenv/resolver.py`) prepends a mirror source built from `PIPENV_PYPI_MIRROR` via `replace_pypi_sources(...)` — and that mirror URL is where the user's credentials live.
- The **parent process** writes the resolver's netrc in `_set_resolver_netrc` (`pipenv/utils/resolver.py`) from `project.pipfile_sources()`, which does **not** include the mirror substitution.

So the mirror's credentials never reached the netrc. Pip then received the mirror URL with credentials stripped from argv and found no matching netrc entry → `401` → `ResolutionFailure`.

This is a different path than #6670 (which handled `${VAR}` placeholders in `[[source]]` URLs and netrc ordering); this one is the `PIPENV_PYPI_MIRROR` env var being skipped entirely when building the resolver netrc.

## Fix

`_set_resolver_netrc` now applies the same `replace_pypi_sources(..., create_mirror_source(...))` substitution the resolver subprocess uses, so the mirror's credentials flow into the netrc again — restoring pre-2026.6.0 behavior without putting secrets back on argv.

## Tests

Adds `test_set_resolver_netrc_includes_pypi_mirror_credentials`, a unit regression test mirroring the issue's config (a custom-host source named `pypi` with credentials only in `PIPENV_PYPI_MIRROR`). Full `tests/unit/test_credential_safety.py` suite passes (17 passed).

## Note

The install-time source builder (`get_source_list`) only substitutes the mirror for `pypi.org/simple` sources, whereas resolution always prepends it. The canonical authed-mirror case (Pipfile source `https://pypi.org/simple` + mirror) already gets credentials into the install netrc and works; the reported failure is at resolution, which this fixes. Broadening `get_source_list` to honor `PIPENV_PYPI_MIRROR` for arbitrary custom-host sources would be a separate behavior change.

title: fix(update): re-lock all Pipfile entries when no packages are given (#6672)
body:
## Summary

- Fixes #6672. Since 2026.0.0, `pipenv update` (no args) silently became a no-op when relaxing a Pipfile pin — the lockfile stayed at the previously pinned version even when the spec allowed newer releases.
- Root cause: gh-6455 routed `do_update` through the partial `upgrade()` path, which only re-resolves Pipfile entries whose locked version no longer satisfies the spec. Relaxing `urllib3 = "<2.7.0"` → `urllib3 = "*"` doesn't trigger that condition because `2.6.3` still satisfies `*`.
- `docs/commands.md:241` describes `pipenv update` (no args) as `lock + sync`. This PR restores that semantics by routing `do_update` through `do_lock` when no packages/editables are given, scoped to the same categories `_prepare_categories` would pick (default + develop on `--dev`, default otherwise). The targeted `pipenv update <pkg>` flow is unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] New unit tests in `tests/unit/test_update.py` covering: no-args routes through `do_lock`; `<pkg>` routes through `upgrade`; `--dev` locks default + develop; default locks default only; `--outdated` still bypasses both paths.

title: fix(auth): Pipfile creds win netrc; expand env vars in pylock sources (#6670)
body:
## Summary

Closes #6670 — restores authentication to private indexes when `[[source]]` URLs use environment-variable placeholders, regressed in 2026.6.1 by the GHSA-8xgg-v3jj-95m2 fix.

- **netrc precedence**: `write_credentials_netrc` wrote our Pipfile-derived `machine` blocks BEFORE the appended existing user netrc. Python's `netrc.authenticators()` returns the LAST matching entry, so any stale system entry for the same host silently overrode the freshly-expanded creds. Reverse the order so our blocks come last and win the tie-break.
- **pylock expansion**: `PylockFile.convert_to_pipenv_lockfile` assigned `self.data[\"sources\"]` raw, dropping env-var expansion on the `[pipenv] use_pylock = true` path. Mirror the legacy `Lockfile.load` behavior by running `expand_url_credentials` over each source URL.
